Covered packaging options (managed listing vs joint solution), network/auth integration (VPC, SAML, KMS), performance validation and shared benchmarks, and next steps for documentation and pilot scheduling.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we know you all have busy calendars so we'll try to be efficient. agenda: marketplace listing + joint reference arch + perf validation.
[00:14] Priya - Aurora: thanks alex, Nora and I will kick off with marketplace constraints, but first quick intro, im priya from infra, marcus handles partner ops.
[00:30] Marcus - Aurora: yep, hi all. we've been talking to product about a joint listing that bundles cedar networking and your inference runtime, also curious about dedicated vs hosted offering.
[00:45] Jenn (SE): cool, we'll outline options. quick callout: we typically support three integration patterns for marketplace listings: 1) hosted API link listing, 2) managed private offering (VPC peering + dedicated capacity), 3) joint solution packaged as a deployable reference arch in the partner marketplace. each has different onboarding steps and compliance requirements.
[01:10] Ethan - Aurora (Security): can you walk through encryption/KMS and audit logs for the managed/private option? our compliance team requires customer-managed keys and full audit trails.
[01:28] Diego (Redwood): yes, for Private we support KMS integration and HSM-backed key management. audit logs are available via our Console and we can stream logs to Aurora's logging sink via secure syslog or S3. there may be minor mapping work for field names.
[01:50] Priya - Aurora: what about network? we prefer VPC peering to avoid public ingress for customer traffic.
[02:00] Alex: agreed, VPC peering works. for the Dedicated offering we can place a dedicated GPU pool in Aurora region; peering + private link can be used. need rough CIDR and peering contact info from priya.
[02:20] Nora - Aurora (Marketplace PM): marketplace listing flow question: what artifacts do you need? screenshots? reference arch doc? a packaged AMI/container?
[02:33] Alex: good question. For a marketplace joint solution we typically submit: reference architecture doc, deployment guide (Terraform/ARM/CloudFormation examples), a validated container image or listing for our managed endpoint, and a short demo video. we'll share the template.
[02:50] Marcus: ok, about billing — if we do a managed offering, how does revenue share/billing work?
[03:01] Alex: typically marketplace handles billing and settlement, we can align on pricing and Redwood will provide metering logs. if it's a joint SaaS + managed solution we can support billing via marketplace or direct contracts depending on partner preference.
[03:18] Ethan: for security review, we'll need SOC2, pen test report, and details about SSO / SAML flows. how do you support SSO for partner admin?
[03:30] Jenn: we integrate with SAML/SSO and support SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is configurable at the org and team level. we'll attach our security pack and a short guide on SAML setup.
[03:48] Priya: latency is a big one for our enterprise customers; they want sub-100ms token latency for short prompts. how do you tune for that?
[04:00] Diego: a few levers: model variant selection, quantization profile, batching configs, prefix/KV cache warmers, and dedicated capacity. for real-time constraints we recommend pinning to a low-latency model and dedicated nodes with warm caches. we'll propose a benchmark plan.
[04:20] Marcus: do you support fallback routing in case of capacity issues?
[04:26] Jenn: yes, smart routing can fall back to compatible model variants or different capacity tiers. policies are configurable per-route.
[04:38] Nora: there was a note about validator tests — can you expand on what you validate before listing?
[04:46] Alex: our marketplace validator checks: functional correctness (sample prompts/evals), latency & throughput benchmarks against stated SLAs, security posture, and a packaging checklist (docs, deployment, monitoring). for joint solutions we add integration smoke tests (VPC peering, SSO auth, KMS key access).
[05:10] Ethan: who runs the benchmarks, you or us? we want reproducibility.
[05:17] Jenn: usually SE runs initial run and shares scripts; then we ask partners to run tests in their environment and compare. we'll give a perf harness (k6/python scripts) and target workloads.
[05:35] Priya: ok can you outline the perf harness? we prefer something containerized we can run in our CI.
[05:42] Diego: it's a small container that hits a set of endpoints with realistic prompt mixes, measures p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and memory usage. we'll push the docker and example config.
[05:58] Marcus: timeline-wise, partner PM wants listing live in marketplace by end of Q2. is that doable?
[06:06] Alex: it's tight but feasible. plan: share docs/template this week, perform integration and perf tests mid-March, iterate on security questionnaire, and aim for listing publish in late June.
[06:24] Nora: dependencies: compliance sign-off, marketplace legal T&Cs, and product screenshots.
[06:30] Ethan: one more on private deployments: does Redwood support on-prem air-gapped installs?
[06:36] Jenn: yes, we have an on-prem package with offline install scripts and options for air-gapped deployment; requires a partner engineering engagement and support contract.
[06:50] Priya: how much engineering time should we expect for a reference arch integration?
[06:56] Diego: initial integration typically 4-6 engineer-weeks for VPC peering, SSO, KMS mapping, and the smoke-tests. faster if you accept managed Redwood endpoints.
[07:10] Nora: naming & branding: marketplace wants co-branded tile and short description. do you have a copywriter?
[07:18] Alex: we'll provide marketing copy + two screenshot sizes. Nora we'll send the copy and ask for Aurora product name confirmation.
[07:32] Marcus: are there any known limitations with the NVidia GPU variants or specific quantization? some of our customers demand int8 models for cost reasons.
[07:44] Jenn: we support quantized variants and can recommend model-specific profiles; we maintain performance profiles for each model+hardware combo. int8 is generally safe for many models but we'll run quality checks.
[07:58] Ethan: audit logging format — can you deliver logs in a schema we can ingest? we use a specific event format.
[08:07] Diego: yes, we can map our audit fields to your schema; expect one-time field mapping work. logs can be exported in JSONL to S3 or streamed via HTTPS to your collection endpoint.
[08:25] Priya: about deployment templates - you mentioned terraform examples?
[08:30] Alex: yes, we'll provide terraform modules that set up peering, roles/iam, and sample service route configs that reference your marketplace account.
[08:42] Nora: question on support SLAs post-launch: we typically require a 24/7 on-call and a two-hour P1 ack. can Redwood commit?
[08:52] Jenn: our enterprise support plan includes 24/7 on-call and P1 ack windows; we can align on escalation and runbooks.
[09:03] Marcus: ok great. Nora and priya will work on packaging requirements.
[09:10] Alex: i'll summarize and send the artifacts. any blockers?
[09:16] Priya: none from infra, just timelines.
[09:20] Ethan: security will review security pack once received.
[09:24] Nora: we'll schedule a follow-up in two weeks to review the ref-arch draft.
[09:31] Alex: perfect. recap of next steps then and owners. thanks everyone.
[09:40] -- end of recording --
